steps.title: What a breakout looks like
steps.text:
A **breakout** is when price **closes** beyond a range or key level and keeps going.

Look at the volume bars too: strong breakouts often come with **higher volume** than the range before them.

steps.explanation: It's the first candle to **close** above resistance. Before that, price was still inside the range.

steps.title: The fakeout
steps.text:
A **fakeout** (false breakout) pokes beyond a level and then closes back **inside**.

It traps traders who jumped in early. When they rush to get out, their orders can push price sharply the other way.

steps.title: Telling them apart
steps.text:
No signal is certain, but these help:

• Wait for a **candle close** beyond the level, not just a wick.

• Look for **volume** above normal.

• Watch the **retest**: a real breakout often comes back to the level and holds.

• Check the **bigger picture**: breakouts in the direction of the higher-timeframe trend tend to work better.

steps.question: Price pushes above resistance during the hour, but the candle closes back below it. What is that most likely?
options: A possible fakeout: the close didn't confirm the breakout
steps.explanation: Only the wick went above the level. Without a **close** beyond it, the breakout isn't confirmed.

steps.question: Which breakout is generally more convincing?
options: A wick above resistance on very low volume
A breakout in thin holiday trading
A close above resistance on higher-than-usual volume
steps.explanation: A **close** beyond the level shows it held for the whole period, and **volume** shows many traders took part.

steps.title: Protect yourself
steps.text: Even good breakouts fail sometimes. Keep your stop on the **other side of the level** (or below the breakout candle), and size the trade so a failed breakout is just a **small, planned loss**.

points: A **breakout** is a close beyond the level that keeps going.
A **fakeout** pokes through and closes back inside.
Failed breakouts happen: always use a **stop**.
